q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of steel scaffolding?
title: Steel scaffolding carbon footprint per tonne
short: Start with the steel tubes and fittings per tonne of scaffolding and the steel supplier's figure. Add cutting, welding, galvanising or painting energy, then divide the plant's energy by tonnes dispatched.

ul: Couplers, base plates and cup locks.

p: Report per tonne by system type. Scaffolding is reused across many jobs, so a site can spread the figure over its life.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per tonne (one month)
lines: Plant total: 91,500 / 2,000 = 45.8 kg CO2 per tonne
Add steel tube and zinc for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
